title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. That is his own version of what Drinfeld (1990) later formalised as the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^.

- Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of the sphere minus 3 points. It is free profinite on two generators, with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1.
- Ŝ^+_{0,3} is an extension of S_3 by Π̂_{0,3}: Π̂_{0,3} = Ker(Ŝ^+_{0,3} → S_3), a kernel–cokernel sequence of Birman type. In it, ρ is an element of order 3 and σ_∞ an involution acting by the anharmonic symmetries.
- φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a fixed homomorphism.
- The objects studied are the u (in a group M^!_{0,3}) that commute exteriorly with φ̂.

Previous page. Such u are encoded by 'normalised' triples (α, β, f). These satisfy:
- the loop relation (11): ξ ≐ η l_1^ν, with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ_∞ρ(β)^{-1}, and 2ν+1 a unit;
- the normalisation (10): φ̂(ξ) = β σ_∞^i.

This page.
1. Since β lies in Π̂_{0,3}, the kernel of the projection to S_3, the integer i is intrinsically determined by ξ.
2. Let φ̂· : Π̂_{0,3} → S_3 be φ̂ composed with the canonical projection (12). Then (10) gives (13): φ̂·(ξ) = σ_∞^i, with i ∈ Z/2Z.
3. This forces an intrinsic condition on ξ: its image under φ̂· must lie in the order-2 subgroup {1, σ_∞}.
4. Grothendieck identifies Ker φ̂· as the normal subgroup N generated by l_0^2, l_1^2, l_∞^3. So φ̂· is the quotient of Π_{0,3} onto the (2,2,3) triangle group, which is the dihedral group of order 6, i.e. S_3. It sends l_0 and l_1 to transpositions and l_∞ to a 3-cycle.
5. Hence the condition reads ξ ≡ l_1^i mod N, i.e. ξ ∈ N ∪ l_1 N. This tacitly uses φ̂·(l_1) = σ_∞.
6. Finally, (10) lets one eliminate β, namely β = φ̂(ξ) σ_∞^{-i}, and replace α by ξ. This leads to the next page's parametrisation of the u by pairs (ξ, f) subject to:
   - (14) ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, a hexagon/3-cycle type relation;
   - (15), the loop relation written purely in ξ.

Purpose. To reduce the description of automorphisms of the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller data commuting with φ̂ to a single element ξ satisfying GT-type equations, together with an inner-automorphism parameter f.
errors: The machine transcription's 'i ∈ Z/12Z' should read 'i ∈ Z/2Z' (see previous page and the subgroup {1, σ_∞}); the mathematics is consistent with Z/2Z.
The identification 'ξ ≡ l_1^i mod N' tacitly assumes φ̂·(l_1) = σ_∞. This depends on conventions for φ̂ not stated on this page; otherwise the step is correct.

The claim Ker φ̂· = ⟨⟨l_0^2, l_1^2, l_∞^3⟩⟩ is correct: the (2,2,3) triangle group is dihedral of order 6. This holds provided φ̂· is surjective onto S_3 with the stated images of the generators. In the profinite setting the normal subgroup should be understood as closed.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms that commute exteriorly with φ̂ by an element ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} satisfying a cocycle/hexagon relation and a loop relation
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (pairs (λ, f) with 2-cycle, 3-cycle/hexagon relations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sketch of the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q)); details unpublished

ideas.what: Determination of i ∈ Z/2Z by the image of ξ in S_3; the kernel of Π_{0,3} → S_3 is the normal closure of l_0^2, l_1^2, l_∞^3
ideas.modern_name: (2,2,3) triangle-group quotient / anharmonic S_3 cover of P^1 minus 3 points

ideas.what: Eliminating β and α in favour of ξ to obtain the conditions ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 and the loop relation
ideas.modern_name: normalisation of GT elements (f ∈ F̂_2 with 3-cycle relation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's own normalisation constraint is that ξ lie in N ∪ l_1 N, where N = ⟨⟨l_0^2, l_1^2, l_∞^3⟩⟩. This is a mod-S_3 reduction condition on the GT-type element, phrased via the (2,2,3) quotient. It is a minor variant of known constraints (e.g. f in the derived subgroup) rather than a new result.
missed.quote: la condition envisagée signifie donc que modulo ce sous-groupe, ξ est de la forme l_1^i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld formulation of GT. It is mathematically elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step in Grothendieck's unpublished pre-Drinfeld derivation of GT-type equations: an elementary reduction mod S_3 and elimination of auxiliary data. It is historically interesting, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'la donnée (α, β, ρ)' should be '(α, β, f)'.
The marginal '417' above Z/2Z is probably a cross-reference (e.g. 'p. 41?'), not part of the formula.
